thread:
AlexW: Quick heads-up — planning a multi-region failover load run for the AcmePOC tomorrow 9:00am PT. Goal: exercise burst + sustained QPS, validate cross-region latency SLOs, and collect token-cost delta for bursting behavior. Need: load script, target QPS/arrival pattern, expected p95/p99 targets, and a short pricing note for the customer. Also flagged: Acme wants confirmation about VPC egress and cert pinning — Ben can you chime in?

Rita_Sales: 👍 thanks Alex. Customer expects a 10k concurrent users spike for 2 min, sustained 1k QPS otherwise. Can we show cost delta for 2-min bursts vs steady? They want a short slide for procurement.

SamInfra: I can provision the load runners in us-west2 and eu-west1. Proposal: two-phase run — ramp to baseline 1k qps over 5m, hold 30m, then 2x burst windows (10k for 2m) with 10m cool-down. Will add 95/99 latency collectors.

MayaEng: For accuracy, use workload mix: 70% short chat messages (avg 40 tokens), 20% long-complete (avg 300 tokens), 10% embedding calls. Embedding calls should go to dedicated endpoint to avoid queuing.

BenSupport: On VPC egress: Acme is in a private VPC and will use Private deployment with NAT egress controls. We need to confirm outbound IPs for their firewall. Also cert pinning: we support customer-managed certs in Private; for Hosted we'll provide TLS from our edge only.

AlexW: Good. Sam — can you post a sample k6/vegeta command so we can sanity-check traffic pattern? Small snippet is fine.

SamInfra: Here's a quick k6 script snippet I'll use:```js
export let options = {
  stages: [
    { duration: '5m', target: 1000 },
    { duration: '30m', target: 1000 },
    { duration: '2m', target: 10000 },
    { duration: '10m', target: 1000 }
  ],
  thresholds: { 'http_req_duration{p100}': ['p(95)<2500', 'p(99)<5000'] }
};
```
I'll parameterize payloads for token sizes.

Rita_Sales: Perfect. Can someone draft a one-slide pricing blurb: cost for steady 1k QPS for 30m + burst delta for those 2x2m windows (estimate using per-token hosted pricing + burst capacity surcharge)? Need it by EOD.

MayaEng: Quick back-of-envelope: assume avg token per request = 80, token cost = $0.0003/token (hosted), baseline: 1k qps * 60s * 30m = 1,800,000 requests => tokens = 144M => ~$43k for that window. Bursts: 10k qps * 2m = 1.2M requests * 80 tokens = 96M tokens per burst => ~$28.8k per burst. Two bursts = ~$57.6k. Total token cost ~ $100k (very rough). Add infra surcharge ~10% for burst capacity. I'll formalize numbers.

BenSupport: Also call out that Dedicated pricing would be flat reserved + smaller marginal for burst via burst pool — might be cheaper for them if they need repeated bursts. I'll add a comparison line.

AlexW: Great. @deploy-bot can you schedule the load run tomorrow 09:00 PT and post the runner IPs to the thread when ready?

deploy-bot: Scheduled load run: 2005432100-run-1 at 2026-03-22T16:00:00Z (09:00 PT). Runners: provisioning in progress. Logs will be posted to /runs/2005432100.

SamInfra: Runners up — k6 cluster nodes in us-west2 (10x m6i.large) and eu-west1 (6x). I'll attach the control command before the run.

SamInfra: Control command:```bash
k6 run --vus 10000 --duration 00:49:00 multi_region_test.js --out json=results.json
```

MayaEng: Quick QA: ensure KV cache warmup for long-complete paths to avoid cold-start p99 spikes. We'll run a 5m warmup with low qps before the main sequence.

Rita_Sales: I'll prep the slide with numbers and risk notes ('short test, not production SLA, cert/egress pending'). Will ping procurement separately.

AlexW: Final checklist: 1) load script + payloads (Sam/Maya) 2) pricing slide (Rita/Maya) 3) firewall egress IPs + cert note (Ben) 4) run scheduled (deploy-bot) 5) post results + p95/p99 + cost delta within 2 hours of run (Sam). Thanks team :rocket:
